items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Public APIs are documented and most names are clear. But the new batch fields (commitJobID, applyDuration, syncStart…) have no comments. onBatchDurable's job eviction, expiredJobs/expiredOrder and the isExpiredLocked range logic also have almost no explanation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: applyInternal gained about 80 lines that build BatchDurableInfo twice, copy-pasted between the sync and NoSyncWait branches. The logic lives in db.go, not the commit pipeline. Counters are tracked twice (durableCommitCount vs totalDurableCommits). getDurabilityManager lazily initialises the manager.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Magic constants 4096, 1024 and 50000. getDurabilityManager does an unlocked nil-check-then-assign, which can race. The NoSyncWait goroutine reads batch.commitErr and fsyncWait after the caller may have closed or reused the batch. Each failure fans the error out to every subscriber; otherwise errors are handled.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API changes are additive. But NoSyncWait sync commits now start a goroutine per commit (`go func(){ batch.fsyncWait.Wait() ...}`) and fire BatchDurable. Every sync commit takes the manager mutex, and every commit pays for applyStart timing even when BatchDurable is unset.
